extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, researchers and readers concerned with publication integrity
extracted.subtask_description: Practices, investigative steps, and policy measures for detecting, preventing, and remediating fraudulent or subverted peer review carried out by editors or others. Focuses on verification, auditing, re-review, and adherence to COPE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on creating fraudulent reviewer accounts / subverting peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must not create fake reviewer identities and use those accounts to submit favorable review reports; Hindawi identified three Editors who appear to have subverted the peer review process by creating fraudulent reviewer accounts and using these accounts to submit favorable review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This behavior is a direct abuse of the editorial process; publishers should investigate suspected cases, contact the involved individuals, and take corrective actions (re-review, retraction, institutional reporting) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active verification of reviewer identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial staff should actively verify the identity of every reviewer who takes part in peer review; Hindawi's staff actively verified email accounts to ensure they belonged to the intended reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification is especially important when review reports are submitted from personal (rather than institutional) email accounts. Active checks (email validation, institutional affiliation checks) should be routine to prevent fraudulent reviewer accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat personal email accounts as higher risk and verify ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Review reports submitted from personal email addresses (rather than institutional ones) were treated as potentially concerning; Hindawi actively verified these accounts to ensure they belonged to the intended reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When personal emails are used, perform additional checks (confirm identity via institutional webpages, phone calls, or other independent contact methods) before accepting reviews at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic analysis / audit of manuscript tracking system log files
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should systematically analyze manuscript tracking system log files to identify potentially concerning cases; Hindawi analyzed logs from 180,000+ manuscripts to uncover abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automated and manual analysis of logs and metadata (submission/reviewer account creation timestamps, IP addresses, unusual reviewer patterns) to detect anomalies. Flagged manuscripts should be individually reviewed by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective review of manuscripts handled by suspect editors
rubrics_metrics.description: If an editor is suspected of creating fraudulent reviewer accounts, investigate all previous manuscripts handled by that editor to look for similar cases of abuse; Hindawi investigated all previous manuscripts handled by the three identified Editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a comprehensive retrospective audit for patterns of irregularity, not just single-instance checks, to assess the scope of potential abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent re-review of suspect published articles (COPE recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent members of journal editorial boards should re-review articles flagged as potentially accepted on the basis of fraudulent reviews; COPE recommended independent re-review of the 32 published articles identified by Hindawi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-review should be carried out by individuals independent of the original handling editors; decisions about suitability for publication should be based on the re-review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retract articles found unsuitable after re-review, according to COPE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If independent re-review determines that an article is unsuitable for publication, it should be retracted; Hindawi will work with COPE to ensure any necessary retractions are handled in accordance with COPE guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE procedures for retraction notices, transparency about reasons, and communication with authors and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult and collaborate with COPE and institutions in investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should consult with the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and provide detailed investigation reports to the institutions of implicated editors so they may conduct their own investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage COPE for recommended processes and involve authors' and editors' institutions for parallel or follow-up inquiries to determine motivations and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement preventive editorial procedures (active reviewer verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should enact procedures designed to prevent abuse, most importantly having editorial staff actively verify the identity of every reviewer who takes part in peer review for any journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change editorial workflows to include identity checks, deny unchecked account creation by editors, and centralize verification tasks to reduce the risk that individual editors can bypass safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid enabling author-suggested reviewers without safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing authors to suggest potential reviewers can be a primary vulnerability enabling fraudulent reviews; Hindawi noted it does not enable author-suggested reviewers, which reduced that particular risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If systems permit author-suggested reviewers, implement strict independent verification and oversight of suggested reviewers before use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit unchecked editorial discretion in reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving editors free rein to solicit any reviewer without independent verification can be exploited; prior to the investigation, Editors were free to solicit reviewers at their discretion, which exposed a vulnerability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish oversight mechanisms (secondary checks, centralized reviewer-account controls, audit trails) so that editors cannot unilaterally create reviewer identities or accept reviews without verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain logs and audit trails to detect peer review rings or coordinated fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and analyze submission and review logs to identify rings, patterns of favorable reviews, and other fraudulent activity; the article references prior cases (e.g., a peer review ring uncovered by SAGE) as analogous abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor for suspicious patterns such as repeated positive reviews from the same accounts, rapid positive reviews, or reviewer accounts linked to single editors; use these signals to trigger investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in reporting investigations and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should publicly report investigations and their outcomes (e.g., Hindawi posted a statement and is re-reviewing/retrating articles) and inform stakeholders when fraud is uncovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear public statements, provide rationale for re-review/retraction decisions, and communicate with the community and affected institutions to preserve trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed reports to institutions of implicated editors
rubrics_metrics.description: When editors are implicated in subverting peer review, publishers should provide detailed reports of their investigations to the editors' institutions so those institutions may conduct their own investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver thorough documentation of findings, methods, and evidence (log files, account records) to enable institutional due process and potential disciplinary actions.
